● Kronos' ability to realize expected cost savings from strategic and operational initiatives;

● The extent of the dependence of certain of our businesses on certain market sectors; ● The cyclicality of our businesses (such as Kronos' TiO2 operations);

● Unexpected or earlier-than-expected industry capacity expansion (such as the TiO2 industry);

● Changes in raw material and other operating costs (such as energy, ore, zinc, aluminum, steel and brass costs) or the implementation of tariffs on imported raw materials and our ability to pass those costs on to our customers or offset them with reductions in other operating costs;

● General global economic and political conditions that harm the worldwide economy, disrupt our supply chain, increase material and energy costs or reduce demand or perceived demand for TiO2 and our products or impair our ability to operate our facilities (including changes in the level of gross domestic product in various regions of the world, tariffs, natural disasters, terrorist acts, global conflicts and public health crises);

paragraphs: Listed below are certain risk factors associated with us and our businesses. See also certain risk factors discussed in Item 7 – "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations – Critical Accounting Policies and Estimates." In addition to the potential effect of these risk factors, any risk factor which could result in reduced earnings or operating losses, or reduced liquidity, could in turn adversely affect our ability to service our liabilities or pay dividends on our common stock or adversely affect the quoted market prices for our securities.

Kronos' sales and profitability are largely dependent on the TiO2 industry. In 2025, approximately 90% of Kronos' sales were attributable to sales of TiO2. TiO2 is used in many "quality of life" products for which demand historically has been linked to global, regional and local gross domestic product and discretionary spending, which can be negatively impacted by regional and world events or economic conditions. Such events are likely to cause a decrease in demand for Kronos' products and, as a result, may have an adverse effect on our results of operations and financial condition.

Pricing within the global TiO2 industry over the long term is cyclical and changes in economic conditions worldwide can significantly impact Kronos' earnings and operating cash flows. Historically, the markets for many of Kronos' products have experienced alternating periods of increasing and decreasing demand. Relative changes in the selling prices for Kronos' products are one of the main factors that affect the level of its profitability. In periods of increasing demand, Kronos' selling prices and profit margins generally will tend to increase, while in periods of decreasing demand Kronos' selling prices and profit margins generally tend to decrease. In addition, pricing may affect customer inventory levels as customers may from time to time accelerate purchases of TiO2 in advance of anticipated price increases or defer purchases of TiO2 in advance of anticipated price decreases. Kronos' ability to further increase capacity without additional investment in greenfield or brownfield capacity may be limited and as a result, Kronos' profitability may become even more dependent upon the selling prices of its products.

The global market in which Kronos operates its business is concentrated, with the top four TiO2 producers accounting for approximately 42% of the world's production capacity and is highly competitive. Competition is based on

a number of factors, such as price, product quality and service. Kronos faces significant competition from international and regional competitors, including increasing competition from TiO2 producers in China, who have significant sulfate production process capacity. Chinese producers have also continued to develop chloride process technology, and the risk of substitution of Kronos' products with products made by Chinese producers could increase if Chinese producers increase the use of chloride process technology and improve the quality of their sulfate and chloride products. Some of Kronos' competitors may be able to drive down prices for Kronos' products if their costs are lower than Kronos' costs, including its competitors with vertically integrated sources of raw materials for the chloride process who may have a competitive advantage during periods of high or rising raw material costs or who operate in regions with less stringent regulatory requirements. For example, Chinese competition generally has lower operating costs due to less stringent regulatory and environmental compliance requirements and less expensive energy prices. China has dumped lower cost sulfate process TiO2 into markets Kronos serves. In some cases, Western TiO2 producers have been successful in obtaining anti-dumping duties on Chinese imports such as duties recently enacted in the European Union, Brazil, Saudi Arabia, and other jurisdictions. In addition, some of Kronos' competitors' financial, technological and other resources may be greater than its resources and such competitors may be better able to withstand extended periods of reduced demand or other changes in market conditions. Kronos' competitors may be able to respond more quickly than it can to new or emerging technologies and changes in customer requirements. Further, consolidation of Kronos' competitors or customers may result in reduced demand for its products or make it more difficult for Kronos to compete with its competitors. The occurrence of any of these events could result in reduced earnings or operating losses.

Many of the markets CompX serves are highly competitive, with a number of competitors offering similar products. CompX focuses its efforts on the middle and high-end segment of the market where it feels that it can compete due to the importance of product design, quality and durability to the customer. However, CompX's ability to effectively compete is impacted by a number of factors. The occurrence of any of these factors could result in reduced earnings or operating losses.

paragraphs: We are primarily a holding company. We operate in the component products industry through our majority-owned subsidiary, CompX International Inc. We also own a noncontrolling interest in Kronos Worldwide, Inc. Both CompX (NYSE American: CIX) and Kronos (NYSE: KRO) file periodic reports with the SEC.

CompX is a leading manufacturer of engineered components utilized in a variety of applications and industries. Through its Security Products operations, CompX manufactures mechanical and electronic cabinet locks and other locking mechanisms used in postal, recreational transportation, office and institutional furniture, cabinetry, tool storage and healthcare applications. CompX also manufactures wake enhancement systems, stainless steel exhaust systems, gauges, throttle controls, trim tabs and related hardware and accessories for the recreational marine and other industries through its Marine Components operations.

We account for our 31% non-controlling interest in Kronos by the equity method. Kronos is a leading global producer and marketer of value-added titanium dioxide pigments. TiO2 is used for a variety of manufacturing applications including coatings, plastics, paper and other industrial products.

paragraphs: 本公司主要為一間控股公司。本公司透過持股過半之子公司 CompX International Inc. 從事零組件產品產業之業務。本公司亦持有 Kronos Worldwide, Inc. 之非控制性權益。CompX (紐約證券交易所美國交易所: CIX) 與 Kronos (紐約證券交易所: KRO) 均會向美國證券交易委員會 (SEC) 提交定期報告。
CompX 為一間領先之零組件製造商，其產品應用於多種應用領域與產業。透過其安全產品部門，CompX 製造機械與電子櫃鎖及其他鎖定機制，應用於郵政、休閒運輸、辦公與機構傢俱、櫥櫃、工具儲存與醫療應用領域。CompX 亦透過其海洋零組件部門製造浪浪增強系統、不銹鋼排氣系統、儀表、油門控制、_trim tabs 及相關硬體與配件，應用於休閒船隻及其他產業。
本公司以權益法計入對 Kronos 31% 非控制性權益。Kronos 為一間領先之全球價值增加型二氧化鈦顏料製造與行銷公司。二氧化鈦 (TiO2) 用於多種製造應用，包括塗料、塑膠、紙張及其他工業產品。

paragraphs: 下列為與我們及我們業務相關的某些風險因素。請參閱第 7 項「管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析－關鍵會計政策與會計估計」中討論的某些風險因素。除了這些風險因素的潛在影響外，任何可能導致營收減少或營運虧損，或流動性減少的風險因素，可能會進一步影響我們償付負債或支付普通股股息的能力，或對我們證券的市場報價產生不利影響。
Kronos 的銷售與獲利 largely 依賴於 TiO2 行業。在 2025 年，Kronos 約 90% 的銷售額來自 TiO2 的銷售。TiO2 用於許多 "生活品質" 產品，其需求歷來與全球、區域及地方的毛貿易總值與自由支配開支相關，而這些可能因區域或世界事件或經濟狀況而受到負面影響。這些事件可能導致 Kronos 產品需求減少，進而對我們的營運成果與財務狀況產生不利影響。

全球 TiO2 行業的價格長期而言具有週期性，全球經濟條件的變化可能顯著影響 Kronos 的獲利與營運現金流。歷來，Kronos 產品的市場經歷過增加與減少需求的交替時期。Kronos 產品的銷售價格相對變化是影響其獲利水平的主要因素之一。在需求增加的時期，Kronos 的銷售價格與毛利通常會增加，而在需求減少的時期，Kronos 的銷售價格與毛利通常會減少。此外，價格可能影響客戶的存貨水準，因為客戶可能在預期價格上漲前加速購買 TiO2，或在預期價格下跌前延後購買 TiO2。Kronos 在不增加綠地或現有廠區容量的情況下進一步增加產能的能力可能受到限制，因此 Kronos 的獲利可能更加依賴其產品的銷售價格。
Kronos 運作的全球市場集中，前四大 TiO2 生產商佔據約 42% 的世界產能，且市場高度競爭。競爭基於

多種因素，例如價格、產品品質與服務。Kronos 面對來自國際與區域競爭者的重大競爭，包括來自中國 TiO2 生產商的競爭增加，這些生產商擁有顯著的硫酸製程生產能力。中國生產商也持續發展氯製程技術，如果中國生產商增加使用氯製程技術並提升其硫酸與氯製程產品的品質，Kronos 產品被替換的風險可能增加。部分 Kronos 的競爭者可能因其成本低於 Kronos 的成本，而壓低 Kronos 產品的價格，包括那些擁有垂直整合原料來源的競爭者，他們在原料成本高或上漲期間可能擁有競爭優勢，或在監管要求較不嚴格的地區運作。例如，中國的競爭通常因監管與環境合規要求較不嚴格及能源價格較低而運作成本較低。中國已將成本較低的硫酸製程 TiO2 傾倒至 Kronos 服務的市場。在某些情況下，西方 TiO2 生產商已成功取得針對中國進口的反傾銷稅，例如最近在歐盟、巴西、沙烏地阿拉伯及其他司法管轄區實施的稅收。此外，部分 Kronos 競爭者的財務、技術及其他資源可能高於 Kronos 的資源，這些競爭者可能更能承受長時間的需求減少或其他市場條件的變化。Kronos 的競爭者可能比 Kronos 更快對新興技術或客戶需求的變化做出反應。此外，Kronos 競爭者或客戶的併購可能導致其產品需求減少，或使 Kronos 更難與競爭者競爭。任何這些事件的發生都可能導致營收減少或營運虧損。
CompX 服務的許多市場高度競爭，許多競爭者提供類似產品。CompX 將努力集中在中高階市場，因為它認為在產品設計、品質與耐用性對客戶重要的情況下，它能與競爭者競爭。然而，CompX 能否有效競爭受到多種因素的影響。任何這些因素的發生都可能導致營收減少或營運虧損。
